explanations.explanation: Right on the money, baker. Haggai 2:20 says it's "the second time that day," on the twenty-fourth day of the month. Haggai, a prophet, gets two words from the LORD before the sun goes down. I'd be tired just carrying the mail.

Close, but the text doesn't make him wait. Haggai 2:20 says "For the second time that day," so no days pass at all. Haggai, a prophet, gets both words on the twenty-fourth. Nobody has to check the mailbox for three days.

A whole month would be a long wait, friend. But Haggai 2:20 says "For the second time that day, the twenty-fourth day of the month." Haggai, a prophet, hears from the LORD twice in one day. No calendar flipping needed.
That's it, baker. The LORD says, "I am about to shake the heavens and the earth." (Haggai 2:21) He's not talking about one wall or one field. That's the whole kitchen AND the whole planet.
Good guess, since walls are easy to picture. But the LORD says He's about to shake "the heavens and the earth." (Haggai 2:21) The text names no walls here. It's much bigger than any wall, friend.

Fields are a fair guess for a land like Judah. But the message to Zerubbabel, the governor of Judah, says "I am about to shake the heavens and the earth." (Haggai 2:21) The fields aren't named. The shaking is way bigger than one farm, baker.
I see why you'd go there, but it's the opposite. The LORD says, "I will overturn royal thrones." (Haggai 2:22) Nothing there about protecting them. Those thrones are getting flipped, baker.

Yes, baker, it's false. The LORD says, "I will overturn royal thrones and destroy the power of the kingdoms of the nations." (Haggai 2:22) He doesn't protect them, He overturns them. Big thrones, bigger flip.

Yep, there's a second part. The LORD says, "I will overturn royal thrones and destroy the power of the kingdoms of the nations." (Haggai 2:22) Thrones go over, and the kingdoms' power goes down with them. It's a two-part promise, baker.

It's true, friend. The same sentence that says "I will overturn royal thrones" keeps going: "and destroy the power of the kingdoms of the nations." (Haggai 2:22) So the thrones are one thing, and the kingdoms' power is the other. Both are in there.

Right, baker. The LORD says, "horses and their riders will fall, each by the sword of his brother." (Haggai 2:22) Each rider falls by the sword of his own brother. That's what the text says, so I'll leave it right there.
Judah is where Zerubbabel is governor, so I get the guess. But the text doesn't name Judah's sword. It says, "horses and their riders will fall, each by the sword of his brother." (Haggai 2:22)

An angel with a sword is a big picture, friend, but it isn't in this verse. The LORD says, "horses and their riders will fall, each by the sword of his brother." (Haggai 2:22) The sword belongs to a brother, not an angel.

That's the word, baker. The LORD says, "I will take you, My servant, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel." (Haggai 2:23) Zerubbabel is the governor, but the LORD calls him "My servant." I'd frame that title and hang it by the oven.
Prophet is a fair guess, since Haggai is right there. But Haggai is the prophet in this scene. The LORD tells Zerubbabel, "I will take you, My servant." (Haggai 2:23)

I get it, since a priest sounds holy and official. But the LORD doesn't use that word here. He says, "I will take you, My servant, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel." (Haggai 2:23) The word is servant, friend.

Yes, baker! The LORD says, "I will make you like My signet ring." (Haggai 2:23) A signet ring is the kind of thing that stamps a seal. As a stamper myself, I take that one a little personally, in the best way.
A staff is a nice picture, but it's not the one here. The LORD says, "I will make you like My signet ring." (Haggai 2:23) Zerubbabel gets a ring, friend, not a staff.
After all those swords in verse 22, I see the pull. But the LORD says, "I will make you like My signet ring." (Haggai 2:23) Zerubbabel isn't made like a sword. He's made like a ring.
That's the one, baker. The LORD says, "for I have chosen you." (Haggai 2:23) The text gives that as the reason for the signet ring. Chosen, plain and simple.
Tested is a fair guess, friend. But the LORD says, "for I have chosen you, declares the LORD of Hosts." (Haggai 2:23) The word is chosen, not tested.
There's a lot of shaking in this message, so warned makes sense. But the reason the LORD gives is this: "for I have chosen you." (Haggai 2:23) He says chosen, baker. That's the word to hold on to.
